label: Customers in PostgreSQL
description: The same customers as @customers/data/customers.store.json, kept in a database rather than in memory. Every word of the declaration is the same -- the collection, the shape, the key, what no two records may repeat, what an added column gives the rows already there -- and only the connection differs. Two stores exist because a profile swaps bindings and not connections (RFC 0002 settled that; RFC 0005 is where it changes), so this is the seam until it does.

customers.description: the customers, one row each, kept per tenant: a caller sees the rows of the tenant their sign-in wrote into the session and no other, no two of a tenant share an address, a note is a field of the customer, and a row written before the tier column reads as bronze

latest.description: the most recent customer registered into each tier, one row per tier: written in the same transaction as the customer itself, so the two cannot disagree. It is not scoped: its key is the tier, which is one row for every tenant, and nothing reads it back

everyCustomer.description: the same rows as customers, every tenant's: the digest, for employees
